title: Molecular Biology Adventure 3: DNA replication, transcription, translation
welcome_lead: Today you'll trace the central dogma — DNA → RNA → protein.
meta_desc: Biology — DNA replication, transcription, translation, genetic code, gel electrophoresis.
final_note: You learned DNA replicates semi-conservatively, mRNA is transcribed in the nucleus, and ribosomes translate codons into amino acids.

Triplet of bases coding one amino acid

walkthroughs.body_html:
Meselson and Stahl (1958) proved DNA replication is semi-conservative.

At the replication fork:
- Helicase unwinds the helix.
- DNA polymerase III adds dNTPs 5'→3'.
- Leading strand continuous, lagging strand in Okazaki fragments joined by ligase.

RNA polymerase binds the promoter and reads the template strand 3'→5', building mRNA 5'→3'.

RNA uses uracil (U) not thymine (T). In eukaryotes, the pre-mRNA is spliced — introns removed, exons joined — and a 5' cap and poly-A tail added before nuclear export.

At the ribosome, each codon on mRNA pairs with a tRNA anticodon.

The codon AUG is the start codon (methionine). The 64 codons encode 20 amino acids — the code is degenerate (multiple codons per amino acid) and universal (same in nearly all life).

Nature of science: Nirenberg cracked the code by synthesising poly-U mRNA (1961).

mcqs.q: Which enzyme unwinds the DNA double helix?
AUG codes for which amino acid (and serves as start)?
How do insulin and glucagon work together to regulate blood glucose?
options: Insulin and glucagon both lower blood glucose using different mechanisms.
Insulin destroys glucose in the bloodstream so it cannot be used.
Insulin works on muscles and glucagon works on the brain.
They are antagonistic — insulin lowers blood glucose (cells take up glucose, store as glycogen); glucagon raises it (glycogen broken back down to glucose).

mcqs.q: What makes antibodies effective against pathogens?
options: Antibodies are tiny knives that physically cut pathogens apart.
Antibodies are general-purpose proteins that work against any pathogen.
Insulin works on muscles and glucagon works on the brain.
They have a specific shape complementary to antigens on a particular pathogen, marking it for destruction or neutralising it.

mcqs.q: What does insulin do to blood glucose?
options: Insulin raises blood glucose to give the body energy.
It lowers blood glucose by causing cells (especially liver and muscle) to take it up and store it as glycogen.
Insulin destroys glucose in the bloodstream so it cannot be used.
Insulin works on muscles and glucagon works on the brain.
